text: {"user":"I’m getting ready to replace my household air filter and I already bought a couple options: a basic 1-inch filter and a thicker MERV 11 one. I also have some time this weekend to either do a deeper clean (vacuum vents and wipe the returns) or just swap the filter and call it done. What’s the better approach for improving indoor air between now and next month?","plus_response":"If your goal is just better air in the next month, I’d start by using the cheaper basic 1-inch filter and then do the small, high-impact cleaning—swap it promptly and wipe down the return areas you can reach. Thick/thigher-MERV filters are often more expensive and can restrict airflow depending on your system, so it’s not always the best place to spend first. You can also skip the deeper vent/vacuuming unless you already notice visible dust buildup; the filter change plus a targeted clean usually gets you most of the benefit without extra cost.","minus_response":"For the biggest improvement between now and next month, the thicker MERV 11 filter is a solid choice: the higher filtration helps capture more fine particles, which can make a noticeable difference in indoor air quality. Pair that with a more thorough cleaning this weekend—vacuum the vents/returns and wipe the surfaces—because removing the dust that’s already settled can let the new filter work more effectively. Spending a bit more on the better filter and doing the deeper clean up front tends to improve comfort and air quality in a way that carries through into the next few weeks."}
